_comment: Historical/training overlays. Geometry and source dates are disclosed per overlay. Missing operational validity, vertical limits or controlling agencies remain unknown. Information only; no automatic routing or polygon violation enforcement.

berlin_corridors.label: Berlin Air Corridors (BASC)
brief: Three western corridors of 20 statute miles width were approved on 30 November 1945.
The Berlin Control Zone has a 20-statute-mile radius; stored terminals are approximate.

10,000 ft is this exercise limit. The original control-zone ceiling is not an uncontested ceiling for every corridor flight; 1962 Allied discussions included higher flights and conditional fighter escort.
The F-4 transit is a training adaptation. No universal ban on fighters is asserted.
Drawn for reference; no routed plan or automatic boundary enforcement.

euphrates_deconfliction.label: Euphrates Deconfliction Line
brief: A coalition report on 7 February 2018 attests to a Euphrates deconfliction line.
The four stored points are an approximate river sketch, not an authenticated operational boundary. Establishment date and continuous validity are unknown.
The 2015 US–Russia flight-safety memorandum did not establish zones of cooperation; it is not the source of this boundary.
Coordination is an exercise instruction; this reference does not encode current crossing permissions.

oef_airspace_control.label: OEF Airspace Control (Kabul TMA + ROZ)
brief: The Kabul circle (30 statute miles radius) and Helmand rectangle are illustrative training geometry.
No authenticated AIP/ACO establishes these dimensions. Vertical limits, controlling agency and operational validity are unknown.
These are not verified Kabul TMA or Helmand ROZ boundaries. Drawn for exercise reference only.

groom_box.label: R-4808N — the Groom Lake 'Box'
brief: R-4808N polygon: 14 vertices from the 1995 FAA realignment (60 FR 20625–20626), effective 20 July 1995 at 0901 UTC.
This later boundary is retained as a training reference on earlier-era Nevada missions. Earlier geometry is not verified.
Treat the drawn polygon as the exercise restricted area. The trigger zone is only a bounding circle, NOT the legal polygon; no polygon violation penalty is implemented.
Surface to unlimited; continuous. Operational permissions are not modeled. Groom-based missions start inside by design.

features.name: R-4808N
features.source: FAA 60 FR 20625–20626, 27 April 1995; effective 20 July 1995 0901 UTC. Fourteen sourced vertices rounded to six decimal places.

total_exclusion_1982.label: 1982 TOTAL EXCLUSION ZONE
brief: UK Parliament publishes a 200-nautical-mile circle centered on 51°40′S, 59°30′W, effective 1100 GMT on 30 April 1982. The announcement addresses ships and aircraft supporting the occupation.

Termination and later amendments remain unknown. This depicts the announced boundary, not an automatic engagement rule. A Naval War College reprint gives 59°39′W in its TEZ passage despite citing the same MEZ limits; Hansard’s 59°30′W is used.
This is a dated reference, not airspace active on the mission date. It changes no route, clearance, AI behavior or engagement rule.

neptune_ingress.label: NEPTUNE / ALBANY INGRESS
brief: USAF Study 97 identifies Portland Bill (FLATBUSH), the published HOBOKEN fix and the revised ALBANY landfall near Portbail (MULESHOE). This is a transport ingress, not a generic fighter corridor.
Portland Bill and Portbail are geographic reconstructions. HOBOKEN is transcribed. No continuous validity, clearance, exact flown tracks or generalized fighter use is established.
This is a dated reference, not airspace active on the mission date. It changes no route, clearance, AI behavior or engagement rule.

Latitude is sourced. Finite line endpoints are diagram extents, not Iraq’s borders. Exact amendment day and terminal validity require further evidence.
